approach: Add a required `dependents` list to a plan. Each entry has `name` (what the plan changes), `dependent` (the code, rule or host setting that relies on it), `kind` (code, rule or host_setting) and a `test` or a `reason` it is unaffected. It goes into `PlanOutput` (and its JSON schema), into the stored `JobPlan` record, and into the text the critic and producer read. `plan_findings` in `admission.rs` refuses a plan with no dependents, a blank name or dependent, or an entry with neither a non-blank test nor a non-blank reason. Each refusal is a Major finding, so the plan goes back to the planner with no critic call. `PlanOutput.dependents` is `#[serde(default)]`, so a plan that omits the key reaches the admission refusal and is revised; the schema still requires the key, because `harden` requires every property. `JobPlan.dependents` is `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]`, so stored records without it still parse and re-serialize byte for byte. `plan_body` renders a "Dependents:" block only when the list is non-empty, so the text and hash of old plans do not change. `planner.md` and `critic.md` gain the rule and the question, each within the budget. A small pure helper, `dependents_unnamed(dependents, hit_paths)`, lists the search hits that no entry names. A replay test searches the real `athena-core/src` for the changed behaviour (`exit_code`), shows that `verify.rs` (the seen-commands filter in `judge`) is among the hits, and checks that the helper reports it unless an entry names it. `refusal_corpus.rs` gets a plan-side case table that drives `plan_findings`. The system-facts budget lines, CHANGELOG and the design doc are updated.

decisions.choice: Refuse in `plan_findings` as a Major Athena finding (location `dependents`).
decisions.reason: Athena's own plan checks already send a Major finding back to the planner with no critic call and no round used (`planning.rs` `RoundEnd::Mechanical`). The rule is enforced by mechanism, not prose, and costs no model call.

rejected.option: Make `dependents` required in serde, so a missing key fails deserialization.
rejected.why: `planning.rs` turns that into 'the planner returned no valid plan' and stops the job. It would not be a revisable finding and could not name the missing section.

rejected.option: A Minor finding, or only a critic question.
rejected.why: A Minor finding does not block, and a critic question is prose. The request asks for a refusal.

decisions.choice: Entry shape: `name`, `dependent`, `kind` (enum code | rule | host_setting), `test: Option<String>`, `reason: Option<String>`. Output and record types are mirrored, as for `PlanRisk` and `PlanFile`. A blank string counts as absent.
decisions.reason: It matches the producer design kept from job 20261102-063419-0beg. It reuses the `Option` pattern of `fails_without` and `seam`. A closed `kind` lets the critic tell host settings from code.

rejected.why: Admission could not check that each dependent has a test or a reason.

rejected.option: One 'evidence' field holding either a test or a reason.
rejected.why: It cannot say which of the two was given, and the brief asks for 'a test and a reason'.

decisions.choice: `JobPlan.dependents` uses `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]`, and `plan_body` prints the block only when non-empty.
decisions.reason: Stored records have no dependents key, so they must still parse and re-serialize identically (the existing seam and resumed_from tests show this pattern). The producer-section hash of an old plan is unchanged.

rejected.why: It changes old record bytes and the hashes in `producer_section_sha256`, and the out-of-scope list forbids migrating records.

decisions.choice: Keep the production check structural. Add a pure `dependents_unnamed(dependents, hit_paths)` helper that is used by the CI-reuse replay test. Do not add a repository search to `plan_findings`.
decisions.reason: The planner searches the repository (the out-of-scope list rules out computing dependents by static analysis). `plan_findings` has no repository access besides `is_directory`, and changing its signature would touch every caller. The replay test shows, on the real sources, that the seen-commands rule is found by search and is unmet unless named.

rejected.option: Make admission grep the repository for the changed names.
rejected.why: Admission does not know what the plan changes, and it would be static analysis, which is out of scope.

decisions.choice: Add plan-side cases to `refusal_corpus.rs` that call `plan_findings`. Do not add a `check_*` step to `refusing_check`.
decisions.reason: The corpus's gate and `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` cover reading checks. The new rule is a plan check, so its input forms (empty list, blank name, neither test nor reason, complete) are plan shapes. Criterion 8 then has a corpus test that fails if the rule is absent.

rejected.option: Put the rule in `reading.rs` as a reading check.
rejected.why: Plans do not exist at reading time.

decisions.choice: The 'what else does this break' question goes in `critic.md` as its own bullet, and the critic brief carries the dependents through `plan_body`.
decisions.reason: The critic needs the list in front of it to compare against a repository search. `plan_body` is already shared by the critic brief, the revision brief and the producer section. There are 483 tokens of critic headroom.

rejected.option: A new constant and section in `briefs.rs`, like `SOUNDNESS_QUESTION`.
rejected.why: The critic prompt is the place the other role questions live. A section would add brief text with no extra enforcement.

risks.risk: The CI-reuse rule is shown by a replay test and prompt text, but nothing in production searches the repository, so a planner could still list dependents that miss one.
risks.mitigation: The limit is stated in the docs and CHANGELOG as prose-only for completeness. The structural check (present, named, with a test or reason) is enforced, and the critic is told to compare the list with a Grep. The out-of-scope list rules out automatic computation.

risks.risk: The stricter rule refuses plans that were fine before. The brief expects about 15% newly refused readings and calls the higher refusal rate intended.
risks.mitigation: It is a revisable Major finding with two mechanical passes, not a stop, and the CHANGELOG states the intent. Stored plans are not re-checked, which the out-of-scope list confirms.

risks.risk: Adding a field to `JobPlan` changes record bytes or breaks a record test or doc.
risks.mitigation: `skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty"` keeps old bytes. The round-trip tests in step 1 cover it. `docs/records.md` and `docs/ontology.toml` do not mention `seam` or `resumed_from`, so I expect no doc check for the new field.

risks.risk: The replay test depends on `verify.rs` text and on a source walk, so it could become brittle.
risks.mitigation: It asserts only the one filter expression and that `verify.rs` is a hit. It does not require every hit to be named. A deliberate change to that filter should update the test.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests in the `admission.rs` test module. Build a `JobPlan` with a reading whose only criterion is Content, so no seam or demonstration rule fires. Vary only `dependents`: empty; an entry with a blank name; an entry with neither test nor reason (also whitespace-only strings); a complete entry with only a test; a complete entry with only a reason. Assert on the returned findings.
demonstrations.observes: An empty list gives exactly one Major finding, with source Athena, location `dependents`, and a summary naming the missing dependents section. A blank name gives a Major finding naming that entry (for example 'dependent 1'). An entry with neither test nor reason gives a Major finding naming the entry's `name`. Complete entries, test-only or reason-only, add no finding. The existing `seam_findings` fixtures now carry a complete entry, so their `is_empty()` assertions still hold.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the dependents rule an empty list adds no finding, so the 'one Major finding naming the missing section' assertion fails, as do the blank-name and no-test-or-reason assertions.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `athena_core::admission::plan_findings(&JobPlan, &Reading, &Policy, &dyn Fn(&str)->bool)`, which is `pub` and called from `run/planning.rs`. Its guards are the demonstration, seam and path rules, which the fixtures satisfy: Content criterion, no files. Fixture: `JobPlan` literals built in the test module, injected as arguments (`findings_for_path` and `seam_findings` already do this). The plan is real data and no part of the rule is in a double. The helper that builds the plan with a `dependents` argument is added in step 6; the call path exists today.

demonstrations.method: Replay test in the `admission.rs` test module. It walks the real `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/src` tree for `.rs` files and keeps those containing `exit_code`. The needle is built as `["exit","code"].join("_")` so the test source does not match itself. It asserts that `src/verify.rs` is among the hits and that its text still holds the filter `c.reused && c.exit_code.is_none()`. It then calls `dependents_unnamed` on two dependents sections.
demonstrations.observes: A section naming only `checks.rs` and the `reused` record leaves `crates/athena-core/src/verify.rs` in the unnamed list, so the requirement is unmet and the test asserts that. A section with an entry whose `dependent` text names `verify.rs`' seen-commands filter (`judge`) and a test leaves it out, so the requirement is met. Other hits (such as `status.rs`) are not asserted either way. The test is part of `cargo test -p athena-core`.
demonstrations.fails_without: If `dependents_unnamed` ignored names, or `verify.rs` were not found by the search, the assertion that the incomplete section leaves `verify.rs` unnamed fails. If the filter were removed from `verify.rs`, the source assertion fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `athena_core::admission::dependents_unnamed(&[PlanDependent], &[String]) -> Vec<String>`, a pure function that step 6 adds. Fixture: the real `athena-core/src` files, read from disk via `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` and not a copy. The `PlanDependent` values are built in the test. No double is used. The guard is that the section names a path or file name. The search itself is the test's own walk; production does not run it (see the open questions).
